answer: A sybil farm mints identities in a burst, planting a thousand saplings in a garden overnight, none tended like a cedar that takes seasons to root. Charge each new identity a creation fee that is burned, not staked, and let the fee rise steeply with how many identities share a funding trail in the same window. One genuine newcomer crossing the ocean alone pays almost nothing; a farm minting a thousand at once pays a fortune, because every extra identity is an echo of the last and pushes the price higher. Spreading the mint over weeks costs the farm the speed its attack needs.
